facts.text: I am a J-1 nonimmigrant physician who has received a waiver based on section 214(l) of the Act.
I will be employed at a qualifying cap exempt institution, organization, or entity pursuant to 8 CFR 214.2(h)(8)(ii)(F)(4).
I have been counted against the H-1B cap.
I am applying for the remaining portion of the 6-year period of admission.
I am seeking an extension beyond the 6-year limitation based upon sections 104(c) or 106(a) of the American Competitiveness in the Twenty-First Century Act (AC21).

My petition is exempt from the numerical limitation for H-1B classification because the petitioner is an institution of higher education as defined in section 101(a) of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (20 U.S.C. 1001(a).

My petition is exempt from the numerical limitation for H-1B classification because the petitioner is a nonprofit entity related to or affiliated with an institution of higher education as defined in 8 CFR 214.2(h)(8)(ii)(F)(2).

My petition is exempt from the numerical limitation for H-1B classification because the petitioner is a nonprofit research organization or a governmental research organization as defined in 8 CFR 214.2(h)(8)(ii)(F)(3).
My petition is exempt from the numerical limitation for H-1B classification because my employer is subject to the Guam-CNMI cap exemption pursuant to Public Law 110-229.
I will be assigned to work at an off-site location for all or part of the period for which H-1B classification is sought.
I will be paid the higher of the prevailing or actual wage at any and all off-site locations.
My petition is requesting an amendment to or extension of stay for my current H-1B classification.
The petition form referenced is Form I-129, L Classification Supplement to Form I-129, Edition 11/02/22.
The referenced USCIS form has OMB No. 1615-0009 and expires 11/30/2025.
